newsitem.title: USA: Exide, Tadiran sign joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Exide, Tadiran sign joint venture.

text.p: Exide Corp said Thursday it signed a memorandum of understanding with Tadiran Ltd, an electronic equipment maker in Israel, for a lithium battery joint venture.

Exide said the pact could lead to the co-development, production and marketing of lithium batteries worldwide. Lithium batteries, used to power cellular phones, computers and other wireless data communication tools, represent a burgeoning market that is growing 20 percent to 25 percent annually, said Exide.
Exide said it hopes to combine Tadiran's development capabilities and technology with Exide's worldwide marketing reach.
The memorandum of understanding was signed by Arthur M. Hawkins, chairman and chief executive officer of Exide, and Israel Zamir, CEO of Tadiran, on February 26 in Israel, said Exide.
Exide, based in Bloomfield Hills, is a major producer of automotive and industrial lead-acid batteries. Tadiran is based in Holon, Israel.
